title: Endpoint Consistency PRD and Gradual Rollout Checklist (chat / completions / embeddings / rerank)
creator: Sofia Moreno
description: High-level PRD to define behavioural contracts, performance SLAs, and a phased launch checklist for the unified hosted endpoint surface covering chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank. Focus is on removing ambiguous edge cases, documenting compatibility expectations across model variants, and specifying operational acceptance criteria required for a controlled, gradual rollout.
goals: Define clear API contracts for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints (including streaming and sync semantics)
Establish compatibility rules for model variants and versioning (backwards-compatible vs breaking changes)
Specify SLOs and performance targets (p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, and token-cost guardrails)
Create an actionable launch checklist with gating criteria for canary -> beta -> GA phases
Ensure observability, automated regression detection, and rollback criteria are in place before wider rollout
non_goals: Redesigning SDK surface — SDK adjustments are tracked in separate tickets
Major changes to storage architecture for embeddings — optimization work will be separate
Replacing existing Dedicated/Private routing logic — this PRD targets Hosted endpoints only
scope_included: API behaviour: request/response contracts, streaming chunk formats, error codes
Compatibility semantics: model aliasing, pinned-model behavior, and fallback rules
Performance SLOs for each endpoint type and recommended default rate-limits
Acceptance test harness and evaluation prompts for quality/regression detection
Launch gating checklist and migration guidance for existing customers
scope_excluded: Console UI changes for rollout toggles (separate console workstream)
On-prem deployment packaging — Private deployment parity will be tracked separately
Billing model changes or pricing updates
api_contracts: Chat: streaming-first semantics over HTTP chunked responses; final delta field must be present in final chunk; function-calling schema must be supported for both streaming and non-streaming modes
Completions: deterministic completion boundaries when max_tokens reached; finish_reason values must include 'length'|'stop'|'invalid_request'|'function_call'
Embeddings: stable vector dimensionality per model; embedding checksum header in response for quick client-side validation
Rerank: stable score normalization (0..1) and deterministic tie-breaking rules; allow batch scoring with preserved input order
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests cover positive and negative request flows for each endpoint (coverage > 85%)
Performance: p95 latency for chat/completions under nominal load <= 220ms for small models, <= 700ms for large models; embeddings p95 <= 180ms for small vectors
Load: service sustains 2x projected peak traffic in canary region without increased 5xx error rate
Quality sanity: no more than 2% prompt-response regressions on curated evaluation set between candidate and control models
Compatibility: older pinned model aliases continue to resolve to expected binary variant for 90 days post-launch unless explicitly migrated
Streaming contract verified: partial-chunk sequence numbers monotonic and final chunk contains 'finish_reason' and cumulative metadata
Rerank determinism: identical input + model version returns identical scores across repeated requests within 48 hours
Embeddings checksum: client-side checksum validation passes for >99.9% of produced vectors in canary
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Internal QA): deploy candidate runtime to staging, run smoke tests, run automated evals against golden prompts
Phase 1 (Canary - internal services): route 1% of production traffic from internal apps to canary region with automatic rollback on increased error or >3% quality regressions
Phase 2 (Limited Beta): invite select external customers (3 customers across different workloads) for 3 weeks; provide dedicated support channel and collection of prompt sets for continuous eval
Phase 3 (Regional Expansion): enable progressive enablement in 2 additional regions with adaptive throttling and monitoring dashboards visible to SRE and PM
Phase 4 (GA): full region enablement, public docs published, migration notes and deprecation windows announced
Rollback Criteria: sustained 5xx increase >0.5 percentage points for 30m, or quality regression >5% on core evaluation set, or latency p95 > 2x baseline for 15m
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboards: per-endpoint p50/p95/p99 latency, 4xx/5xx rates, token-per-second throughput, and cost-per-token telemetry
Quality Alerts: regression detector that raises P1 if evaluation set drift >3% for 1h
SLO Alerts: burn-rate monitor tied to weighted SLOs across endpoints; auto-create incident on sustained burn-rate >2x for 30m
User-impact Alerts: synthetic clients exercising streaming and rerank paths with end-to-end latency and result checksum — alert when mismatch or slow responses detected
dependencies: ENG-84210: runtime streaming chunk metadata & sequence number implementation
ENG-84721: model aliasing and pinned-version resolution service (compatibility guarantees)
ENG-85500: embeddings storage format v2 (checksum header support)
DES-6812: API error UX spec for client-visible error codes
SEC-1290: security review for public endpoint headers and rate-limiting surface

migration_plan: Notify customers 30 days before GA about potential behavior changes and backward-compatibility windows
Provide a 'compatibility' query parameter that pins legacy behaviour for 90 days post-GA
Offer a migration checklist and sample SDK patch for customers needing streaming -> non-streaming fallbacks
Coordinate with Sales & Success for one-off migration support for top 10 high-traffic customers
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: subtle quality regressions when switching kernel selection for large models. Mitigation: daily eval runs and staged rollout with immediate rollback capability
Risk: client integrations relying on previous streaming chunk shape. Mitigation: feature flagging, compatibility parameter, and 60-day dual-support window
Risk: burst traffic causing token-cost spikes. Mitigation: conservative default rate-limits, adaptive throttling, and cost-anchored alarms
notes: This PRD intentionally focuses on behavioural clarity and rollout hygiene rather than micro-optimizations. Follow-up tickets should track performance tuning and quantization recommendations.
Acceptance criteria include both technical SLOs and product-quality checks (eval-based). Both must be green before moving from Beta -> Regional Expansion.
Ensure legal & compliance review is requested for customers in regulated industries prior to Private parity announcements.
